public_payload.normalized_proposition: As of October 2023 it is still common for LLMs to produce complete falsehoods.

statement.excerpt: 9 months later—an eternity in current AI—it’s stilly common for LLMs to spout complete, utter bullshit.

our_interpretation: In context, complete falsehoods means invented factual assertions presented as true, rather than offensive language or every kind of mistake.
Common means a recurring, non-exceptional problem in ordinary factual tasks. It does not require a majority of all outputs to be false.
The context illustrates the present with last week's and last night's examples. I use September 25–October 4, 2023, the last complete calendar week before publication through the post date.
The nine-month phrase supplies timing, not a conditional antecedent.
Selected anecdotes alone cannot establish frequency. Results confined to one difficult task also cannot establish frequency across ordinary factual uses without qualification.
criteria.support_condition: Repeated evaluations of widely used contemporary LLMs show fabricated factual assertions at nontrivial rates across a reasonably representative range of ordinary factual tasks.
criteria.contradiction_condition: Comparable evaluations show that fabricated factual assertions were exceptional across ordinary factual tasks in the relevant contemporary systems.
